entry.title: Social Summary: November 28, 2026
entry.summary: Community celebration week for the Hermes ecosystem. The headline post is NousResearch's 24-hour Black Friday deal — 50% off the first month of Nous Portal plans with code FIFTYFIFTY — which drew the batch's biggest reach (134k+ views, 893 likes) plus a useful tail of official clarifications: the exclamation mark isn't part of the code, and the discount applies to the first month only. Ecosystem energy centers on rlaope's Oh My Hermes (OMH) plugin, nearing 6.2k GitHub stars, with a power-user report of burning 200B tokens/month on Hermes-Agent, a walkthrough of the dag ulw DAG-orchestration skill that parallelizes subagent-owned jobs, a fresh speedup letting Hermes self-run final checks on small tasks, and a new Terminal Desktop & Bot System release. Founder Teknium stayed highly visible — asking the community about reusable audit skills, advising users to point agents at resources to build from, and spreading holiday cheer. Sentiment is warm and builder-heavy: Thanksgiving gratitude led engagement (1,519 likes on the official thank-you to Hermeticists, 602 on Teknium's greeting), and rlaope's striking 'hermes' image pulled 310 likes. (One low-scored link-only reply to @Albinkultur was excluded due to a corrupted record ID in the source data.)

entry.title:
oh-my-hermes turns Hermes into a graph engineer, and as of this week it's a faster one.
oh-my-herme...
entry.summary: Announces a performance improvement to oh-my-hermes, the plugin that plans Hermes Agent jobs as a graph of subagent-owned pieces run in parallel with a separate final check. As of this week, small jobs no longer pay the full graph price: Hermes now runs the final check itself instead of spawning an extra agent, and closes out finished pieces together to avoid round trips, cutting latency and agent count while keeping guardrails. Big jobs still use the full graph. Includes an install/run link for Hermes users.

entry.title:
If you hand Oh-My-Hermes a big job without typing "dag ulw", you're doing it the slow way.
https://...
entry.summary: A detailed walkthrough of the dag ulw skill in the oh-my-hermes workflow layer for Hermes Agent. Typing dag ulw triggers a directed-acyclic-graph planning mode with ultrawork: the goal is stated as a single line, split into independently checkable outcomes, decomposed into graph nodes each owned by a subagent with scoped files and a proving command, then carried end-to-end without pausing to ask the user at each step. The post also recaps oh-my-hermes features like long-term memory, lazily routed expert skills, and per-model tuning, and links to a demo.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 27, 2026
entry.summary: Obsidian Integration Launch (headline story): NousResearch's official announcement that Hermes Agent can now control an Obsidian vault as a private, local shared knowledge base via an official connector leads the section, amplified by Teknium's viral 'Obsidian 🤝 Hermes' post (~1.3k likes, ~42k views). This was the highest-engagement story of the batch and community reaction was strongly positive. Multi-Model Orchestration (hottest builder trend): rlaope's hands-on terminal showcase splitting a plan into five parts and routing across models after Gemini 4 Neon landed in Hermes Agent is the standout demo; community chatter treats Hermes as an orchestration hub across GPT-6.2 Sol, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Opus 5.5, Kimi, and Qwen, with rlaope also tipping Gemini Neon for time-sensitive tasks. oh-my-hermes Ecosystem (expanding fast): oh-my-hermes 5.0.1 adds delegation of coding work to external CLIs (Devin, Gemini, Qwen, Kimi, Cursor, Amp, Droid, Aider, Goose); the omher desktop app showcase ('the window I live in now') and its 6.1k GitHub stars milestone mark a real community-tooling success; a benchmarking plugin built on Hermes Agent's harness beat omp on the same 11 coding tasks. Sentiment is proud-but-collaborative, reinforced by a new Oh-My-Hermes Discord with fast PR merges. Waitlist Growth & Onboarding: Teknium welcomed the new wave of Agent users and disclosed 2000 invites sent in a single day just three weeks into the waitlist, plus visible bug-triage on a herdr model-switching issue — an attentive-maintainer vibe. Human interest: Teknium's firsthand origin story (one gaming GPU → cofounder karan4d) and his candid reflection that half his success came from building in public give the section personality. Filtered out: one-line replies ('I agree', 'Hot damn', 'It's fine'), 'very soon TM' teases, an ad for third-party token-resale service OpenGateway, and three duplicate link-only spam posts.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 26, 2026
entry.summary: Privacy & trust led the week: Teknium celebrated Hermes earning an A grade for respecting user privacy (1,009 likes, 42k views — the standout post), reinforced by official confirmations that telemetry is opt-in in both the Hermes agent and desktop app, and that users can point Hermes at any provider — a cluster of replies that turned a user concern into a trust win. Ecosystem tooling stayed hot as community builder rlaope shipped omher desktop 1.2.1 (a CLI desktop wrapping the Hermes-Agent bot with workflow packs, subagent routing, connectors and skills) and crossed 10,000 commits on the Oh-My-Hermes GitHub. Momentum & teasers: Teknium promised Hermes will be 'running in hyperdrive' (634 likes, ~21k views), while the NousResearch account teased an imminent reveal ('Can't wait to share it with the world', 'Sooon') and name-dropped Nous Portal to a high-profile follower. Product direction & guidance: desktop design unification confirmed in response to user feedback, and Teknium shared that plugin catalog submissions are typically reviewed and cleared within ~3 days — actionable for builders. Industry banter drew strong reach: Teknium's pointed reply to @sama ('3 years late but better late than never'), a nudge to theo to audit closed-source projects next ('quite sad I imagine 😳'), and a widely resonant origin story — hobbyist programmer doing Uber Eats before ChatGPT dropped — plus a warm welcome for notch to the crew. Overall sentiment: proud, shipping-focused, and rallying around privacy as Hermes' core differentiator, with the community celebrating both external validation and its own building cadence.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 24, 2026
entry.summary:
Oh-My-Hermes Desktop & Ecosystem Launch: The standout community story is @rlaope's launch of Oh-My-Hermes (OMHER Desktop), an open-source desktop app built on Hermes Agent that has surged past 6k GitHub stars — 'a face for every bot' featuring a GrokBot companion, with repo and download links shared in-thread. Ecosystem momentum extends across the batch: day-one oh-my-hermes provider support for the newly announced GLM 5.4 (not yet in our model-tracking reference, suggesting a fresh same-week release), a 6k-star Hermes-Agent Plugin milestone thank-you, free Hermes Agent motion reels, and a deep three-day engineering retrospective running Oh-My-Hermes on 3x RTX 6000 Pro — covering SGLang DSA fixes, Triton/FlashInfer kernels, AWQ/GPTQ quantization, a path-traversal security fix, and vLLM KV-cache verification.

Enterprise Strategy & Roadmap: @Teknium delivered the batch's most substantive strategic statement, correcting skepticism in the @pabis_eu thread: Hermes enterprise plans existed from day one, with an enterprise team in place since April and named design partners.
